findings.finding: Regression in cost drivers from the iter-03 changes (node-aligned purlins, deeper trusses, client-requested higher bearing). Linear roof steel is now ~6,384 m, about 2.05x Option A's 3,106 m (A's purlins are understated; see A review A-STR-01). Purlins alone are 2,800 m (350 members, 1.89 m spacing). Roof area is 6,844 m2 (+28% vs A). Taller enclosure: external wall area rose from 4,279 to 5,093 m2 and hall air volume from 30,149 to 40,190 m3 (+33%), so B's advantages in volume and wall area over A (5,824 m2, 49,768 m3) have mostly gone. Roof top is now +17.78 m against A's +18.4 m. Only the column count (56 vs 76) and pad concrete (140 vs 163 m3) remain clearly lower.
findings.evidence: comparisons/out/comparison.md (B03-44bc3ae457, sha256 356464e19ccc094f): Truss 2486.6 m / Purlin 2800.0 m / Bracing 1097.4 m, Roof 6844.1 m2, External wall 5093.0 m2, Hall air volume 40190.0 m3, Roof top 17.78; metrics purlin_count 350, purlin_lines 35
findings.fix: Treat the 5.5 m clearance over the rear passage as a client decision to be costed; test 10 m truss spacing (fewer trusses and purlin bays, deeper purlins) and the narrower hall from the fan study; consider purlins at full panel points (3.79 m) with sheeting rails or deeper-profile sheeting only if the manufacturer confirms the span. Obtain a QS tonnage comparison of A and B once members are sized.

findings.finding: Taller supports raise slenderness and wind demands that the concept does not address. The grid-1 facade columns are 0.40 m placeholders standing ~11.75 m from pad to top, with masonry only to +6.0 and cladding/louvres above. The side-wall posts are 0.40 m and ~12 m tall. The hall side and stage masonry walls are now 13.5 m high, outside the column line, restrained only by posts and columns at ~8-8.8 m centres, with no bond beams or wind girts modelled. The foyer rafter still bears on the truss end post ~3.5 m above the grid-2 column cap, so the end post carries an eccentric reaction.
findings.evidence: STR-COL-F1 bbox z -0.9..10.85 (0.40 x 0.40); STR-COL-A-P3 z -0.9..11.1 (0.40); ENV-WALL-EXT-S top 6.0, ENV-CLAD-S z 6.0-11.74; ENV-WALL-HALL-E height 13.519, ENV-WALL-HALL-N 13.466; STR-BEAM-FOYER-F end (40, 0.0, 12.2) vs STR-COL-F2 top 8.65
findings.fix: Reserve space for horizontal wind girts or bond beams at about mid-height of the 13.5 m walls and the facade cladding zone; flag the facade and side-post column slenderness for the engineer (likely larger sections or intermediate restraint); detail a pinned seating bracket for the rafter on the truss end post, or carry the rafter on the column via a corbel.

findings.finding: Maintenance and erection regressions from the raised roof. The single eaves gutter rose from +7.93 to +11.26..11.61 m, ~7.7 m above the canopy, so it now needs a MEWP or a permanent ladder and anchor line rather than access from the canopy. The overflow weirs discharge over the canopy ends near the covered ambulatory routes. Truss bearings are now +8.8 to +13.3 (column caps 8.65 / 13.29), so lift heights are similar to Option A while the trusses are longer (53 m) and 11 in number. open_issues still lists gutter access only as TBC and models none.
findings.evidence: SRV-GUTTER-S z 11.26-11.61; ENV-CANOPY z 3.6-3.85, x -4.55..84.55; SRV-GUTTER-WEIR-E/W at x ~81 / ~-1, y -13.5; STR-COL-F2 top 8.65, STR-COL-F4 top 13.29; metrics truss_span 53.05; reports/open_issues.md line 14
findings.fix: Model a roof access point (internal hatch or external caged ladder at a gable end) and an eaves anchor line; extend the weir spouts past the canopy ends or into downpipes to the rainwater tank with a visible overflow at grade; add splice locations and crane standing positions to the erection open issue.

findings.finding: No bottom-chord lateral restraint (fly braces or ties) is modelled for uplift reversal on a 53.05 m simply supported truss under a ~5,500 m2 lightweight roof. Lateral load paths now look complete in concept: eaves girders with chords along grids 2 and 4, roof strips AB/EF/FG/KL, end-wall and long-wall vertical bracing, and foyer end-bay bracing. Only the collector from the grid-4 girder to side-wall braced bay 5 (one bay from grid 4) relies on the end-truss chord.
findings.evidence: 30_STR_Bracing families: STR-BRACE-ROOF-{AB,EF,FG,KL,EAVES2-*,EAVES4-*,FOYER-AB,FOYER-KL}, STR-BRACE-WALL-{2AB,2KL,4AB,4KL,A1,A5,L1,L5}; no bottom-chord restraint members; config side_braced_bays [1, 5]
findings.fix: Reserve bottom-chord ties/fly braces at alternate panel points; move the side-wall braced bay from 5 to 6 (adjacent to grid 4), or state that the end truss acts as the collector.

strengths: All iter-01/02 structural premise issues are closed: simply supported Pratt trusses (diagonals top at support -> bottom towards midspan, verified), no back-span uplift, 3.5 m depth (span/depth ~15.2), and every roof-brace node on a purlin/strut line (verified, 0.000 m offset).

Complete concept lateral system for both directions, including eaves wind girders along both long walls and foyer end-bay bracing; the clash matrix passes (BLD-CLASH 0 over 194,191 pairs, with controls); 56 columns / 56 footings.
STR-CLR 5.53 m clear over the rear passage meets the client's request, and it is checked in the model rather than asserted.

Gutter overflow weirs are modelled at the gutter ends, away from the central entrance doors; the single roof plane with no box gutters and the envelope outside the column line remain good buildability choices.
Honest status: open_issues lists splices, erection/crane plan, movement joint, uplift, deflection and gutter access as not designed.
limitations: No loads, rainfall, wind or geotechnical data are available, so member adequacy, slenderness, deflection and uplift could not be assessed; span/depth remarks are rules of thumb. Read-only checks were run on model/blender_manifest.json (truss F nodes and diagonals, brace-node vs purlin alignment, column/footing counts, column, wall, gutter, weir and canopy extents), params.json and the reports; comparisons/out/comparison.md was used for quantities. Renders in renders/B03-44bc3ae457/ and the exports drawings were not inspected in detail. Crane availability in Zimbabwe was not verified.
certification_disclaimer: This review is a structured QA metric for a concept coordination model by an AI reviewer. It is not a professional engineering certification, structural design check, code-compliance statement, fire approval or cost estimate. No loads, analysis or member design were performed; all member sizes in the model are space-reservation placeholders. A registered Zimbabwean structural engineer must design and certify the structure.
